title: CCS5 & TSC: Spacecraft Monitoring & Control Systems
status_notes: Marked PUBLIC, dated 13 March 2024 on the title slide (PDF p. 1); slide footers carry '(c) The Terma Group 2022'.
summary:
A 56-slide public product presentation by Terma, dated 13 March 2024, on CCS5 (multi-user checkout and operations system) and TSC (single-user version for instruments, payloads and SCOE AIT), part of the Terma Ground Segment Suite (TGSS).

It explains the motivation: legacy European systems such as SCOS-2000, OC and CGS were judged hard and costly to maintain, so Terma wrote a completely new implementation that stays compatible with the SCOS-2000 MIB data model (ICD 6.9 to 7.2) and with SCOS-2000 TOPE scripting, so that users need little retraining. Slides list the supported standards (PUS-A and PUS-C, CCSDS packets and CFDP, TM frames, TC CLTU and COP-1, CCSDS 355.0/355.1 SDLS and ESA PSS-04-151 authentication, CubeSat Space Protocol), the MIB extensions (unlimited field lengths, variable packets, deduced parameters in TM and TC, configurable length indicators, endianness, several synthetic-parameter languages), and the EGSE packet-level plugins (EDEN, C&C, serial, CAN, ZMQ, NATS) and MCS frame-level drivers (NIS with optional SLE, Cortex, NDIU LITE, KSAT LITE).

Further slides cover performance figures, Qt/QML displays and mimics, TOPE (Tcl/Tk) automation and debugger, the archive (RDBMS index plus segmented raw binary files with nanosecond time stamps), history browsers and retrieval tools, merging MIBs from several suppliers, SVF mode, TM simulation from the MIB, TC modelling, AutoPilot and fleet views, constellation and Kubernetes cloud deployment, related tools (TRACK, PLAN, STAT), instrument and payload EGSE use cases, user roles, quality process and licensing.

It shows how the SCOS-2000 MIB has become a de facto exchange format beyond ESOC's own software.

contents.title: Complex Use Cases: Advanced Applications for AIT

key_points.text: Terma decided on a fully new implementation of compatible products using the SCOS2000 MIB data model, because legacy European systems (e.g. SCOS2000, OC, CGS) were becoming difficult and uneconomic to maintain; TSC is single user (instruments, payloads, SCOE AIT) and CCS5 multi-user (satellite-level AIT and operations).
The TM/TC features follow and enhance those of the SCOS2000 MIB (ICD 6.9 to 7.2) and support ECSS PUS-A and PUS-C, while PUS is not mandatory.

MIB enhancements include unlimited field lengths, global variable packets and parameters, deduced parameters in TM and TC, configurable length indicators for variable-length parameters, endianness support, automatic TC header time stamps and several synthetic-parameter languages.

EGSE packet-level plugins (EDEN, C&C, serial, CAN, ZMQ, NATS) cannot be mixed in one program, while MCS frame-level protocols (NIS with optional SLE, Cortex, NDIU LITE, KSAT LITE) can be combined in any combination.

Quoted maximum performance: about 150,000 TM parameter updates/s, about 1500 TM packets/s, about 5 Mbit/s monitored housekeeping and 80 Mbit/s unmonitored data, and about 500 TC/s (TSC) or 100 TC/s (CCS) with verification.

TOPE (Test & Operations Procedure Executive) is Tcl/Tk based, with syntax and basic commands derived from SCOS2000 TOPE; it adds session control, TM packet simulation, TC modelling, COP-1 control and frame-level coding and decoding.

Archive indexes are stored in an RDBMS (MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL; TSC uses SQLite), TM parameters are stored on change, raw data is kept in segmented binary files with nanosecond time stamps, and every TC verification stage is recorded.
MIBs from different suppliers (platform, payloads, instruments, EGSE) can be merged, dropped and loaded without restart, with online viewing, search, filter and patch features.
TM packets can be simulated from the MIB definition by inverting TM processing, for example to simulate a platform or act as a SCOE controller.

Built-in security support covers CCSDS 355.0-B-1 and 355.1-B-1 extended procedures (CMAC, HMAC, GMAC, CBC-MAC; ECB, GCM, CCM) and ESA PSS-04-151 hard-knapsack authentication with a 'Sentinel1' CMAC enhancement.
AutoPilot uses NATS publish/subscribe messages carrying JSON or CBOR, supports constellations of up to 9999 spacecraft and is also accessible from Python.
